title: SSC CGL 60-Day Study Plan 2026: 8-Week Schedule with Mocks
description: An 8-week SSC CGL 2026 study plan at 5 hours a day: weekly topic tables for Quant, Reasoning, English and GA, topic tests and a mock schedule.
intro: Sixty days is enough to cover the full CGL syllabus once and still leave two weeks for mocks, **if you start with average basics and study about 5 hours a day**. The plan runs in four phases: arithmetic and verbal base, the advanced Quant blocks, topic tests with weak-area repair, and a mock-only finish.

sections.title: Phases, daily budget and weekly rhythm
sections.body:
| Weeks | Phase | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 to 2 | Base | Speed maths, arithmetic, verbal reasoning, grammar |
| 3 to 5 | Build | Data Interpretation, Geometry, Algebra, Trigonometry, non-verbal reasoning, vocabulary, RC, science |
| 6 | Repair | Topic tests, previous-year patterns, weak areas |
| 7 to 8 | Test | Full mocks, analysis, revision loops |

**Daily budget (about 5 hours):**

| Slot | Hours |
|---|---|
| Quant | 1.75 |
| Reasoning | 1.0 |
| English | 1.25 |
| General Awareness | 1.0 |

**Weekly rhythm.** Days 1 to 6 of each week are study days. Day 7 is the test day: a sectional test (weeks 1 to 4) or a full mock (weeks 5 to 8), then at least 90 minutes of analysis. Add 20 minutes every night to update the mistakes notebook, and read 5 new words a day from the [vocab](/vocab/) page. Working candidates can use the same sequence at 2.5 hours a day over 120 days.

sections.title: Week 6: repair
sections.body:
Use mock 1 and mock 2 to build a ranked list of weak topics. Spend the week like this:

| Day | Plan (5 h) |
|---|---|
| 36 | Weak Quant topic 1: re-learn, 30 questions, timed set (1.75 h); weak Reasoning type (1 h); weak English area (1.25 h); GA (1 h) |
| 37 | Weak Quant topic 2, same pattern |
| 38 | Weak Quant topic 3, same pattern |
| 39 | Re-solve every wrong question from mocks 1 and 2 |
| 40 | Mixed timed sets: 25 Quant, 25 Reasoning questions in 15 minutes each |
| 41 | Mixed timed sets: 25 English and 25 GA questions in 15 minutes each, then formula sheet pass |
| 42 | **Full mock 3**, analysis |

sections.title: Weeks 7 and 8: mocks and revision
sections.body:
No new topics. Mock days follow a fixed routine: attempt at your expected shift time (60 minutes), take a 20-minute break, then analyse for 2 hours. On non-mock days, revise.

| Day | Plan |
|---|---|
| 43 | Revise mock 3 mistakes, formula sheet, vocabulary |
| 44 | **Full mock 4**, analysis |
| 45 | Weak-area drills (2 h), current affairs of the last 3 months (1 h), static GK (1 h), grammar (1 h) |
| 46 | **Full mock 5**, analysis |
| 47 | Revise mistakes notebook, Quant formulas, idioms and one-word substitutions |
| 48 | **Full mock 6**, analysis |
| 49 | Rest half day, light revision |
| 50 | **Full mock 7**, analysis |
| 51 | Weak sections only, 15-minute timed sets |
| 52 | **Full mock 8**, analysis |
| 53 | Current affairs and static GK revision, grammar rules |
| 54 | **Full mock 9**, analysis |
| 55 | Formula sheet, mistakes notebook, vocabulary |
| 56 | **Full mock 10**, analysis |
| 57 to 58 | Light revision only: formula sheet, mistakes notebook, 25 mixed questions a day |
| 59 | Rest; check admit card, ID, centre route |
| 60 | Rest and sleep |

Ten mocks in 15 days is a heavy schedule. If you feel stale, drop one mock and use that day for analysis. Estimate how you stand using the [score calculator](/exams/ssc-cgl/score-calculator/) and compare with the bands on the [cutoffs](/exams/ssc-cgl/cutoffs/) page.

sections.title: Adjusting the plan
sections.body:
- **Weak basics in Quant:** add a week at the start for NCERT-level maths, and shift everything by 7 days. A 90-day plan is a better fit in that case.
- **Strong in Reasoning:** reduce Reasoning to 30 minutes a day and add the time to English or Quant.
- **Tier 1 already in progress or over:** keep the arithmetic and verbal weeks, but switch the mock weeks to Tier 2 style (see the Tier 2 strategy guide).
- **Typing:** from week 5, add 15 minutes of keyboard practice on the [typing test](/exams/ssc-cgl/typing-test/) page. The data-entry speed test is qualifying and needs a few weeks of regular practice.

faqs.q: Is 60 days enough for SSC CGL?
faqs.a: It is enough to cover the syllabus once and take about 8 to 10 mocks, if you can give around 5 hours a day and have average school-level basics. Candidates with weak basics should prefer the 90-day plan.

faqs.q: How many hours should I study per day on this plan?
faqs.a: About 5 hours: roughly 1.75 for Quant, 1 for Reasoning, 1.25 for English and 1 for General Awareness. If you have only 3 hours, extend the plan to around 100 days.

faqs.q: When should I take the first full mock?
faqs.a: At the end of week 4 on this plan, once you have covered most of arithmetic, DI and geometry. Sectional tests in weeks 1 to 3 build the habit of timed solving.

faqs.q: What should I do if I fall behind?
faqs.a: Drop the lowest-frequency topics (Mixture and Alligation, Dictionary Order, Medieval History) rather than the mock days. Mocks give feedback that no extra chapter does.

faqs.q: Can I follow this plan for Tier 2?
faqs.a: Weeks 1 to 6 work as a base for Tier 2 too. For Tier 2, shift more time to English (45 questions) and the harder Quant blocks, and take Tier 2 pattern mocks.
